config.title: Build API key management endpoints

intro.title: Build API key management endpoints
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build secure API endpoints to manage API keys, allowing users to generate, view, and revoke keys for accessing your Node.js application. You'll learn how to handle HTTP requests, validate user input, and interact with a database to store and retrieve key data. The core programming concepts include using Express.js for routing, middleware for authentication, and asynchronous operations for database queries. By the end, you'll have a functional key management system that follows RESTful principles and ensures data security.
intro.usecase: API key management endpoints are essential in any developer portal or admin dashboard where users generate and manage credentials for accessing your services. For example, Stripe's dashboard allows developers to create, view, and revoke API keys for secure payment integrations. Similarly, cloud platforms like AWS or Twilio provide administrative panels where users can rotate keys, set permissions, and monitor usage. As a backend developer, building these secure endpoints ensures controlled access and is a foundational skill for creating scalable, production-ready APIs.

objectives: Construct a Node.js route to generate and store a new API key
Implement middleware to validate API keys on incoming requests
Configure an endpoint to list all active API keys for a user
Manipulate the database to revoke an API key by updating its status
Integrate rate limiting based on API key usage
Apply input validation to ensure secure key generation parameters
Initialize a structured response format for all key management endpoints

steps.instruction: Import Express, body-parser, and uuid by adding the necessary import statements at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the 'require' syntax to import these Node.js packages. Express is the web framework, body-parser helps parse JSON request bodies, and uuid generates unique identifiers for API keys.

steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance, use body-parser middleware to parse JSON, and set up an in-memory array to store API keys.

steps.expectedOutcome: An Express app instance is created, configured with JSON parsing middleware, and an empty array is ready to store API keys.
successCriteria: Express app instance is created, body-parser.json() middleware is applied, and an empty array variable is declared for API keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create POST endpoint for generating API keys
steps.instruction: Define a POST route at '/api/keys' that generates a new API key object with a name and permissions.
steps.hint: Use app.post() to define the route. Inside the handler, create a new key object with an id (use uuidv4()), a name from the request body, and permissions from the request body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route '/api/keys' is defined that will create a new API key object with a unique id, name, and permissions.
successCriteria: The POST route '/api/keys' is defined with a handler that creates a new API key object containing id (generated with uuidv4()), name, and permissions from the request body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the POST route, but make sure the handler creates a complete API key object with id, name, and permissions from the request body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint for generating API keys is not properly defined. Ensure you're using app.post() with the correct route path and creating a new key object inside the handler.

steps.title: Implement API key generation logic
steps.instruction: Inside the POST endpoint handler, replace the comment with code to generate a new API key object containing a UUID-based key, name, permissions, and creation date,
steps.hint: Create an object with properties: id (UUID), key (UUID), name (from request body or default), permissions (from request body or default), and createdAt (current date). Use uuidv4() for UUID generation and new Date() for the timestamp.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST endpoint now generates a unique API key with metadata and returns it as JSON when called.
successCriteria: The endpoint handler creates an object with id, key, name, permissions, and createdAt properties, pushes it to apiKeys, and sends it as JSON response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your object includes all required properties: id (UUID), key (UUID), name, permissions, and createdAt. Also remember to push to apiKeys and send the JSON response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The endpoint handler doesn't yet generate a complete API key object. Review the example: you need to create an object with the specified properties, add it to the apiKeys array, and return it as JSON.

steps.title: Create GET endpoint for specific API key
steps.instruction: Define a GET route '/api/keys/:id' that finds and returns a specific API key from the apiKeys array.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the route containing a parameter ':id', then find the key using find() method on apiKeys array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new GET route '/api/keys/:id' is added that can retrieve a single API key by its ID.
successCriteria: The route '/api/keys/:id' is defined with app.get(), uses req.params.id to find the key, and returns appropriate JSON response.

steps.title: Create DELETE endpoint to revoke API key
steps.instruction: Define a DELETE route handler for '/api/keys/:id' that removes an API key from the apiKeys array based on the id parameter.
steps.hint: Use app.delete() with the route path containing a parameter. Inside the handler, find the index of the key with matching id and remove it using splice(). Send a 200 response on success or 404 if not found.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DELETE endpoint is defined and ready to remove an API key from the apiKeys array when a request is made with a specific id.
successCriteria: A DELETE route '/api/keys/:id' is defined using app.delete() with a handler that attempts to find and remove an API key by id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the DELETE endpoint, but make sure to include the logic to find and remove the key, and handle the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DELETE endpoint is not correctly defined. Check the route path and handler structure.

steps.title: Add error handling middleware
steps.instruction: Add middleware after all your routes to handle 404 errors for unmatched routes.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with a function that takes req, res, and next parameters. Inside, set the response status to 404 and send a JSON error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will respond with a 404 status and JSON error message for any route that doesn't match your defined endpoints.
successCriteria: Middleware is added after all routes, uses app.use(), sets status to 404, and returns JSON with an error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your middleware is placed after all routes and returns a proper JSON response.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added middleware after all routes, set the status to 404, and returned JSON with an error message.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000 and log a message to the console when the server is running.
steps.hint: Use app.listen(port, callback) to start the server. The callback should log a message like 'Server running on port 3000'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express server will start on port 3000 and log a confirmation message to the console.
successCriteria: app.listen() is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a server status message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling app.listen() with both the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're starting the server with app.listen() on port 3000 and logging a message when it starts.
